body:
### Summary

`uv run --with <req> <entrypoint>` stops seeing the `--with` packages when the project venv's path is long. A >127-byte shebang is enough.

- In that case `format_shebang` (`crates/uv-install-wheel/src/wheel.rs`) writes the launcher as an absolute `/bin/sh` wrapper (`#!/bin/sh` / `'''exec' '/abs/.venv/bin/python' "$0" "$@"`).
- `copy_entrypoint` (`crates/uv-project-commands/src/run.rs`) only recognises the *relocatable* `/bin/sh` form and a bare `#!<python>` line, so it skips this form. The trace shows: `Skipping copy of entrypoint .venv/bin/pytest: does not start with expected shebang`.
- The base launcher then runs the base interpreter, and the ephemeral `--with` environment is invisible to it.

The same project at a short path works. The bug shows up only at long paths, e.g. deep git worktrees or CI workspaces.

### Reproduction

```bash
d="$TMPDIR/$(python3 -c 'print("a"*200)')/proj"   # any path giving a >127-byte shebang
mkdir -p "$d" && cd "$d"
uv init -q --bare --name repro
uv add -q pytest
printf 'def test_x():\n    import six\n' > test_x.py
head -1 .venv/bin/pytest                    # -> #!/bin/sh
uv run --with six pytest -q test_x.py       # -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'six'
uv run --with six python -m pytest -q test_x.py   # -> 1 passed (workaround)
```

Run the same steps under a short directory (shebang ≤127 bytes) and `uv run --with six pytest` passes.

### Expected

`copy_entrypoint` should also accept the absolute `/bin/sh` wrapper that uv itself writes for long paths, and rewrite it to point at the ephemeral interpreter.

### Platform / version

- macOS aarch64 (Darwin 27.0.0); uv 0.11.32 and 0.12.17 (same behaviour).
- I read the code on `main` @ c0110fc, and `copy_entrypoint` still matches only the two forms above.
title: `uv run --with` packages invisible to project entrypoints when the venv path forces the /bin/sh shebang wrapper
